transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Dmitri Sokolov (Redwood SE); Anika Patel (Peregrine Head of Cloud Partnerships); Jon Rivera (CTO); Leo Alvarez (Infra Architect); Sofia Martinez (Solution Eng)

Auto-summary (auto gen): Quick partner discovery. Peregrine is an SI/reseller targeting telco and large retail customers; they want a hybrid offering with cloud + on-prem GPU on customer sites. Main asks: private control plane, KMS integration, predictable latency for chat use-cases, and a reseller billing flow.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick intros, we'll keep this to 45ish minutes and then we can schedule a tech deep dive. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Dmitri our SE.
[00:18] Anika Patel: Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Anika, I run partnerships at Peregrine. We're an SI and reseller, we help enterprise customers stand up hybrid models. On the call with Jon and Leo who run the platform and infra.
[00:29] Jon Rivera: yeah hi all. we want to understand how Redwood could fit into our offering, and what the constraints are for on-prem customers.
[00:36] Dmitri Sokolov: great. quick note: we have three deployment modes — hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For reseller scenarios most folks look at Redwood Private or Dedicated with private peering.
[00:51] Leo Alvarez: when you say Private, do you mean we run a customer-managed control plane inside their VPC, or you host a control plane and we just tunnel? we have strict requirements around data residency so we prefer customer-managed control plane.
[01:10] Dmitri Sokolov: yes — Redwood Private can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane. it's configurable. we've done deployments with a private control plane in the customer's VPC and an optional air-gapped package. the control plane talks to your hardware via mTLS and you can plug in your KMS / HSM.
[01:30] Sofia Martinez: a quick practical question: what's the typical footprint to start — like number of GPUs and the stack? our customers vary from a single rack on prem to full cloud fleet.
[01:45] Dmitri Sokolov: common starting point is 4–8 GPUs for a pilot; depends on model size and concurrency. we support batching and kv-cache to reduce cost. if you're serving chat with 2–4k token contexts concurrently you'll want at least 8 A100/RTX-class equivalents in many cases. but we'll benchmark.
[02:12] Jon Rivera: okay, benchmarks — we need some numbers. target latency is user facing chat: 150–250ms p50 for short responses, maybe 400–500ms for long context. is that realistic?
[02:25] Dmitri Sokolov: 150ms p50 is tight for medium-sized models on-prem unless you tune batching aggressively and use quantized kernels — but we can get there with lower context lengths and optimized kernels. for larger contexts you hit KV cache and memory limits. Also there are trade offs: lower latency vs higher cost.
[02:45] Anika Patel: from the reseller side we need a clear matrix — which customers should go hosted vs Private vs Dedicated. we also need clear handoff docs — who supports what.
[02:56] Maya Chen: totally — we'll share a partner playbook template. It includes support boundaries, onboarding flow, ticket routing, and a standard SOW for pilots.
[03:08] Leo Alvarez: security: SOC2 is a baseline for our customers. they also ask for KMS integration, audit logs, SSO with SAML, RBAC. do you have prior SOC2 evidence and an audit log API?
[03:23] Dmitri Sokolov: yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II. we expose audit logs and you can integrate an external KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and on-prem HSMs via KMIP). SSO via SAML or OIDC for Console. logs can be routed to your SIEM.
[03:40] Jon Rivera: good. can we get the SOC2 report and a short security Q&A? we'll need it for procurement.
[03:46] Maya Chen: absolutely, I'll send the security pack after the call.
[03:50] 
[04:10] Anika Patel: commercial — Peregrine resells to customers and wants margin. do you have a reseller discount or channel pricing? and how are credits or committed capacity handled for resellers?
[04:25] Maya Chen: we have channel programs. for early partners we do reseller pricing + co-selling support. For Dedicated/reserved capacity we offer committed contracts and flexible burst. For Redwood Private enterprise licensing is typically a platform fee plus support. We can draft a channel rate card.
[04:45] Sofia Martinez: on billing — can the customer get consolidated billing from Peregrine or do they pay Redwood directly? we need a flow where Peregrine invoices the customer and Redwood invoices Peregrine.
[04:58] Maya Chen: yes, we can support reseller billing flows; we do a principal-agent setup in many cases. we'll put the details in the partner commercial addendum.
[05:10] 
[05:28] Jon Rivera: integration surface: how does routing work? if a customer wants on-prem for sensitive data but fallback to hosted in heavy load, is there an automated routing/failover?
[05:41] Dmitri Sokolov: smart routing is part of our runtime — you can define policies by latency or cost, region, or customer tier. automatic fallback to compatible model variants is supported. the tricky part is KV cache and session affinity — you'll need a strategy for warm/kick caches when failing over.
[06:03] Leo Alvarez: that cache warm-up is a pain for us. can we pre-warm or snapshot caches for known active sessions?
[06:12] Dmitri Sokolov: you can persist and ship KV caches between instances in some deployments; we'll show the options in the technical deep dive. it's not seamless for all model families, but possible.
[06:25] 
[06:35] Anika Patel: use-cases — our customers are telco (virtual agents, call routing), retail (product QA/search), and insurance (document ingestion + claims summarization). We'll triage which ones are latency sensitive vs batch.
[06:52] Maya Chen: nice spread. for ingestion/batch you can use embeddings pipelines + batch embed endpoints, that sits separately from low-latency chat.
[07:05] 
[07:20] Jon Rivera: what about model management and versioning? we need guaranteed pins for model versions in production.
[07:30] Dmitri Sokolov: Redwood supports model pinning and rollout policies — canary/A-B and automatic fallback. model catalog shows performance profiles. you'll be able to pin a model version per-route.
[07:42] 
[08:00] Sofia Martinez: ops — what metrics do you expose? token breakdown, latency per route, per-customer cost, traces? we need traceability for performance SLOs.
[08:13] Dmitri Sokolov: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, p50/p95 latency, per-model dashboards, traces, and error analysis. plus we provide tracing hooks. You can export metrics to Prometheus or Datadog.
[08:30] 
[08:40] Leo Alvarez: network requirements — ports, egress, firewall rules for the control plane? We often can't open broad egress from customer racks.
[08:55] Dmitri Sokolov: control plane talks over mTLS; we publish a minimal port list. For fully air-gapped setups we have an on-prem package but it requires local registry and offline license handshake. We'll share the whitepaper.
[09:10] 
[09:20] Jon Rivera: model footprint: do you have recommended quantization/precision profiles for typical LLMs? our customers sometimes demand fp16 then quantize 8-bit to save cost.
[09:32] Dmitri Sokolov: we have quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize — we recommend dynamic quantization per-workload. we ship profiles and can suggest specific kernels for 4-bit/8-bit. note some evals see small quality regressions; we tie quality monitoring to prompt sets.
[09:52] 
[10:00] Anika Patel: pilot scope: what do you recommend for a first pilot with one of our telco customers — something that proves latency and cost economics?
[10:12] Maya Chen: I'd propose a 6-week pilot: week 0–1 onboarding and infra deploy; weeks 2–4 benchmarks and live shadow traffic; weeks 5–6 rollback and tuning plus final SOW. Success criteria: p50 latency <300ms for targeted flows, error rate <1%, and a cost per 1k messages below agreed threshold.
[10:36] Jon Rivera: that sounds reasonable. we'll need a list of required access and a sandbox environment.
[10:45] 
[11:00] Dmitri Sokolov: we'll need representative traffic — qps, sequence length distribution, burst patterns. if you can share a week of anonymized traces (no PII), we can replay them for the benchmark.
[11:14] Leo Alvarez: we can provide synthetic traces and a scrubbed sample. we'll coordinate offline.
[11:22] 
[11:30] Maya Chen: procurement and legal: we expect standard entitlements — data residency, indemnity, standard SLA. Are there any unusual procurement constraints?
[11:40] Anika Patel: some of our customer contracts require 3rd party vendor background checks and special SOC2 addenda. Also some need specific data retention timelines.
[11:51] Maya Chen: we'll include a procurement FAQ and vendor questionnaire with the security pack.
[11:58] 
[12:10] Jon Rivera: edge cases — multi-tenant hosting where Peregrine wants to manage multiple customers on the same cluster. is it supported?
[12:20] Dmitri Sokolov: multi-tenancy is supported with strong RBAC, per-tenant model pinning, and quotas. you'll want to be careful with shared KV caches and isolation of logs. We can go deeper in the technical session.
[12:36] 
[12:50] Anika Patel: one business question — does Redwood work with downstream marketplace listings so we can list Peregrine as an integrator?
[13:00] Maya Chen: yes we have partner listings and co-marketing programs. we'll connect you with partner marketing.
[13:08] 
[13:20] Dmitri Sokolov: quick note on failover — when you route to hosted from an on-prem, you'll pay attention to model variant compatibility. e.g. quantized local model variant may not be bit-for-bit compatible with hosted floats; fallback may need translation or you keep a compatible hosted variant.
[13:42] Leo Alvarez: ok — that's an operational detail we'll review.
[13:46] 
[14:05] Jon Rivera: for the technical deep dive, we'd want to run a short benchmark: toy model + representative traffic then iterate. How long would that take to set up?
[14:16] Dmitri Sokolov: if we get infra access and a small cluster provisioned, 1–2 days to stand up the runtime and another day for the first run. end-to-end including analysis ~1 week.
[14:30] 
[14:40] Anika Patel: timeline — we want to present to an initial customer pilot target by mid March. does that align?
[14:49] Maya Chen: yes — if we start the pilot SOW by early Feb and do the technical deep dive in the first two weeks of Feb, March pilot start is reasonable.
[14:59] 
[15:10] Jon Rivera: any blockers on our side? we'll need the pilot SOW and security docs to pass procurement.
[15:18] Maya Chen: we'll get those out. I'll send the docs and propose deep-dive slots.
[15:25] 
[15:35] Closing recap (Maya):
- Redwood Private supports customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations.
- We'll send SOC2, security pack, and deployment whitepaper.
- Pilot: 6-week suggested scope, success metrics proposed.
- Action items: Maya sends docs; Dmitri prepares benchmark plan; Peregrine shares workload traces.

[15:50] Jon Rivera: thanks everyone, we'll review and get the traces to you.
[15:55] Anika Patel: thanks, good first call.
[16:00] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: speaker attributions occasionally were generalized; some product names transcribed as slight variants (e.g., "Redwood Private" sometimes appears as "redwood private control"), typical of meeting exports.
notes: This is a partner discovery call. Not all technical details finalized; deeper SE-led bench session planned. Peregrine focused on reseller model and private deployments for regulated customers.
human_summary: Redwood AE/SE met Peregrine Gateway to scope an SI integration: reseller economics, private on-prem deployments with customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM and SOC2 requirements, latency targets for chat, and a 6-week pilot proposal. Security docs and partner playbook to be shared; technical deep dive and benchmarking planned in early Feb.
